results.corrected_claim: ToolbarContent.contentMarginsRemoved(_:) is a new iOS 27 toolbar modifier. Declaration: `nonisolated func contentMarginsRemoved(_ removed: Bool = true) -> some ToolbarContent`. Introduced at 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS, with no deprecation or beta flag. Abstract: 'Configures whether the content margins are removed.' Discussion: 'Use this modifier to remove the default padding around a toolbar item’s content. This is useful for content that goes to the edge of the item.' Apple's sample is `.toolbar { ToolbarItem { CustomButton() } .contentMarginsRemoved() }`. It is not on the SwiftUI Updates page. The skill never mentions it: there is no contentMargin* anywhere under skills/, and references/01-api-reference.md line 298 is the '## 8. Toolbar integration' heading.
results.notes: source_type: apple-doc. I checked the raw declaration tokens (nonisolated, `_ removed: Bool = true`, `-> some ToolbarContent`) and the raw metadata.platforms (seven platforms, all 27.0). The hierarchy puts it under SwiftUI/ToolbarContent, so it applies to toolbar content such as a ToolbarItem, not to a View. I searched all four 100k-character chunks of updates/swiftui.json. Neither the primary content nor the references contain 'contentMarginsRemoved'. The June 2026 'Toolbars' bullets cover only visibilityPriority(_:), ToolbarOverflowMenu, topBarPinnedTrailing and toolbarMinimizationBehavior(_:for:).

results.corrected_claim: TabRole.prominent is new in iOS 27. Declaration: `static var prominent: TabRole { get }`. Introduced at 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS. Abstract: 'The prominent role.' Discussion: 'A tab role that provides prominent visual treatment to one of the tabs in supported tab bars. Only one tab can receive the prominent treatment. When there are no tabs with an explicit .prominent role, then a .search role tab may receive the prominent visual treatment by default.' The SwiftUI Updates page (June 2026 › Tab bars) says: 'Set the prominent role on a tab to place the tab in a separate, trailing position of the tab bar.' WWDC26 session 269 'What's new in SwiftUI' (5:12) shows `Tab(role: .prominent) { CartTab() }`. The skill's tab-bar pattern only uses `role: .search` (patterns/glass-tab-bar.md line 20), and `.prominent` appears nowhere under skills/.
results.notes: source_type: apple-doc for the symbol JSON (raw tokens and platforms checked) and for the Updates page (updates/swiftui.json, June 2026 › Tab bars, quoted word for word). source_type: apple-video for https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2026/269/. Its transcript reads: 'The shopping cart tab is displayed on the bottom trailing edge of the screen ... I'm using the new prominent tab role to make it stand out.' The code block there is `TabView { Tab { EventsTab() } Tab { HolidaysTab() } Tab { FunTab() } Tab(role: .prominent) { CartTab() } }`. `Tab(role:content:)` exists on the Tab page as `init(role: TabRole?, content: () -> Content)`, and title/systemImage variants such as `init(_:systemImage:role:content:)` also take a role. Only one tab can be prominent. Without one, the .search tab may get the treatment by default, so the skill should not claim .search always takes the trailing slot. Blog posts (Swift with Majid, Juejin) were used only as search leads, not as evidence.

results.corrected_claim: NavigationTransition.crossFade is new in iOS 27. Declaration: `static var crossFade: CrossFadeNavigationTransition { get }`. Introduced at 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS. macOS is absent from both metadata.platforms and the declaration's platforms list. Abstract: 'A navigation transition that cross-fades between the appearing view and the disappearing view.' Discussion: 'Specify this transition in a sheet to have it appear by fading in over the content, as opposed to moving upwards to cover content.' Apple's example applies `.presentationDetents([.medium]).navigationTransition(.crossFade)` to the sheet content inside `.sheet(isPresented: $showSheet) { ... }`. CrossFadeNavigationTransition is a struct conforming to NavigationTransition, with the same six-platform availability. The skill's only sheet transition is `.navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:))` (patterns/glass-modal-sheet.md line 64 heading, code at line 74). crossFade appears nowhere under skills/.
results.notes: source_type: apple-doc. I checked the raw tokens and raw platforms of both navigationtransition/crossfade.json and crossfadenavigationtransition.json; neither lists macOS. The SwiftUI Updates page (June 2026 › Transitions) also says: 'Specify the crossFade transition to have a sheet appear by fading in over content.' Code using it in a multiplatform target that includes macOS needs an availability or platform guard.

results.corrected_claim: View.presentationPlacement(_:) is new in iOS 27. Declaration: `nonisolated func presentationPlacement(_ placement: PresentationPlacement) -> some View`. Introduced at 27.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS. Abstract: 'Sets the placement of a presentation within the presenting view.' Discussion: 'By default, a presentation uses automatic placement. Use this modifier to place it on the leading or trailing edge. For example, to maximize the visibility of the primary content behind a presented sheet:' followed by `Map().sheet(isPresented: $isPresented) { PlaceDetailView().presentationDetents([.medium, .large]).presentationPlacement(.leading) }`, then 'Only sheet presentations respect this placement.' PresentationPlacement is a struct (Equatable, Hashable, Sendable) whose only topic group, 'Specifying sheet placement', lists `static let` members automatic, center, leading and trailing. It is not on the SwiftUI Updates page. The skill never mentions it.
results.notes: source_type: apple-doc. I checked the raw tokens, the raw platforms (seven, all 27.0) and the raw topicSections of presentationplacement.json. The member abstracts are: automatic 'The system determines the placement of the presentation.'; center 'Centers the presentation within the presenting view.'; leading 'Places the presentation on the leading edge of the presenting view.'; trailing 'Places the presentation on the trailing edge of the presenting view.' I searched all four chunks of updates/swiftui.json and found no 'presentationPlacement' or 'PresentationPlacement'. The only sheet-related June 2026 bullet is the crossFade one. patterns/glass-modal-sheet.md line 80 is the '### Tall sheet that doesn't dim background' heading.

results.corrected_claim: View.tabViewBottomAccessory(isEnabled:content:) was added in iOS 26.1. Declaration: `nonisolated func tabViewBottomAccessory<Content>(isEnabled: Bool, @ContentBuilder content: () -> Content) -> some View where Content : View`. Introduced at 26.1 on iOS, iPadOS and Mac Catalyst only, not deprecated. Abstract: 'Places a view as the bottom accessory of the tab view. Use this modifier to dynamically show and hide the accessory view.' The isEnabled parameter: 'If true, the bottom accessory is shown; otherwise, the bottom accessory is hidden.' Apple's sample is `.tabViewBottomAccessory(isEnabled: hasStatusUpdate) { HomeStatusView() }`. The original `tabViewBottomAccessory(content:)` (iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst 26.0) now also declares `@ContentBuilder content`. ContentBuilder is documented as `typealias ContentBuilder = ViewBuilder`. The skill only shows `.tabViewBottomAccessory { … }` (references/01-api-reference.md line 379) and never uses isEnabled.
results.notes: source_type: apple-doc. I checked the raw declaration tokens of both overloads; each has an attribute token `ContentBuilder` with preciseIdentifier s:7SwiftUI14ContentBuildera. I checked the raw platforms: isEnabled is 26.1 and content-only is 26.0, both iOS, iPadOS and Mac Catalyst only (not macOS, tvOS, watchOS or visionOS). swiftui/contentbuilder.json confirms the ViewBuilder typealias, so existing @ViewBuilder-style closures still work. A skill that targets iOS 26.0 needs `if #available(iOS 26.1, *)` around the isEnabled overload. Apple's discussion on both overloads says: 'On iPhone, ... when the tab bar is normal size, the accessory appears above it; when the tab bar is collapsed, the accessory displays inline.' This overload is not on the SwiftUI Updates page, which the finding does not claim anyway.

results.corrected_claim: The skill is wrong. TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement (`enum TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement`, introduced at 26.0 on iOS, iPadOS, Mac Catalyst, macOS, tvOS, visionOS and watchOS) has exactly two cases. `case expanded`: 'The bar is expanded on top of the bottom tab bar, if there is a bottom tab bar, or at the bottom of the tab’s content view.' `case inline`: 'The view is displayed in line with the bottom tab bar.' There is no `.collapsed` case. The environment value is Optional: `var tabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement: TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement? { get }` (26.0 on all seven platforms), and its discussion says 'A nil value corresponds to an undefined placement.' The comment `// .expanded | .collapsed` at references/01-api-reference.md line 396 should read `.expanded | .inline`, and the type should be noted as Optional.
results.notes: source_type: apple-doc. I checked the raw topicSections, which list only TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement/expanded and /inline. I also checked the raw tokens of environmentvalues/tabviewbottomaccessoryplacement.json; it ends in `TabViewBottomAccessoryPlacement? { get }`. The likely source of the mistake is Apple's own wording on the tabViewBottomAccessory pages: 'when the tab bar is collapsed, the accessory displays inline'. 'Collapsed' describes the tab bar, and the enum case is `.inline`. The `.collapsed` token appears only at line 396 under skills/. patterns/glass-tab-bar.md line 44 says 'expanded or collapsed' only in prose, and its code (`if placement == .expanded`) is fine. My own reasoning, not from the docs: a `switch` over this Optional value probably needs a `nil`/default case to be exhaustive. Apple's overview sample switches on it with only `.inline` and `.expanded`, and that sample is also missing a closing brace, so the skill should not copy it verbatim.
